description: In October **1962**, the world spent **13 days** on the verge of nuclear war. Missiles in Cuba, fleets on alert: the Cold War reaches its peak.

hero.hook: Thirteen days where a single “yes” could have triggered the nuclear apocalypse.

blocks.text: In October **1962**, humanity comes close to the worst. During **13 days**, the United States and the USSR clash over nuclear missiles installed in Cuba, an island less than 150 km from Florida. The bombers are ready. One mistake, and everything can change.

This crisis is the peak of the Cold War. It takes place in the offices of Washington and Moscow... and also in an isolated submarine, where an officer refuses a shot that could have destroyed everything.

In **1959**, **Fidel Castro** took power in Cuba. For Washington, a Moscow ally so close to the American continent is unacceptable. In April **1961**, the CIA, the American secret service, organized a landing at . It's a disaster. US President **John F. Kennedy** is humiliated. Castro moves even closer to the USSR. [[Bay of Pigs]]
To hide Operation , the secret deployment of missiles, the Soviets also took on board agricultural equipment... and Russian winter clothing, as if the destination was elsewhere. [[Anadyr]]

**Nikita Khrushchev**, the Soviet leader, wants to restore balance. The Americans have already placed  missiles in Italy and , very close to the USSR. He decides to secretly install medium-range missiles on Cuban soil. [[Jupiter missiles in Turkey]] [[Türkiye]]

sections.title: Cuba, too close to the United States

blocks.text: **October 14**, an American U-2 spy plane photographs  missile ramps, capable of reaching a large part of the United States. Kennedy brings together a small crisis committee. For six days, we weighed all the options: bombings, invasion, diplomacy. [[SS-4]]

blocks.caption: U-2 photos reveal Soviet missiles in Cuba.

blocks.text: Generals, like Curtis LeMay, want to strike immediately. Kennedy chose a middle path: a naval blockade. He called it “quarantine” to avoid the word “blockade”, which means war in international law. On **October 22**, on television, he reveals the missiles to the world and demands their removal.

On **October 27**, nicknamed “Black Saturday,” a U-2 is shot down over Cuba. At sea, the Soviet submarine **B-59**, harassed and cut off from Moscow, prepares to launch a nuclear torpedo. The protocol requires the agreement of three officers. Two say yes. **Vasily Arkhipov**, the political officer on board, says no.
The famous “red telephone” installed after the crisis is in reality a **teletypewriter**. The red telephone only exists in movies.

Behind the scenes, an agreement is being made. The USSR withdraws its missiles from Cuba. The United States agrees not to invade the island. Secret clause: American missiles from Türkiye will be withdrawn later.

The crisis opens a phase of, a relative appeasement between the two blocs. A direct line will soon connect the Kremlin and the White House. The [[Détente]] doctrine prevails: since no one can win a nuclear war, no one should start it. [[Mutual Assured Destruction (MAD)]]

blocks.text: In **13 days**, the Cuban crisis shows that the Cold War could destroy the world... and that it sometimes came down to a single refusal, that of Arkhipov.
